algorithm.convergence_criteria: No Monte Carlo replication count, error tolerance, confidence interval, stabilization test, or seed-reproducibility rule is reported.
software: Pseudocode only; no language, random-number generator, seed, array type, or packaged implementation is provided.
steps: Initialize wear to zero.
Loop over simulation time and nominal person index.
Draw body weight and simultaneous-user count from the stated normal distributions.
Draw upward or downward direction using p_up.
Evaluate GRF(weight,direction) and L(weight,direction).
Multiply normal force and sliding distance.
Generate a direction- and crowding-dependent position.
Accumulate alpha times force-distance divided by hardness and multiplied by g into wear[x,y].
Return the wear grid.

assumptions: Body weight and crowding are normally distributed; direction follows p_up; force, sliding distance, and position generators adequately represent each step.
models.computational_cost: Approximately proportional to the time horizon times the number of simulated persons plus grid storage; actual complexity depends on PositionGenerator and GRF implementations.

details: The paper does not specify out-of-grid position handling or stair-edge behavior.
The algorithm accumulates finite-horizon wear rather than solving an equilibrium.
Initialize the wear grid to zero before the nested time-person loop.

constraints: Define integer nonnegative crowding, bounded direction probability, valid grid positions, positive weights, consistent force-distance units, and a finite simulation horizon.

equation_status.reason: Algorithm 1 is source pseudocode rather than a numbered displayed equation; all numbered Equations 1-36 are retained in the preceding model units.

identifiability_feasibility.analysis: The loop is implementable after choosing integer truncation, grid boundaries, sample sizes, units, and generator definitions, but those choices are not specified by the source.

limitations: Crowding draw semantics, integer and nonnegative handling, grid bounds, units, replications, seed, convergence, and independent validation are unspecified.
missing_details: Executable code, distributions fitted from data, truncation rules, position generator, force and sliding functions, random seed, replication error, and parity fixture.
objectives: Generate spatial wear realizations and a cumulative wear field under stochastic pedestrian use.

parameter_estimation.method: Normal distributions are assigned to body weight and simultaneous-user count and a Bernoulli draw uses p_up; estimation samples and uncertainty are not supplied.

models.purpose: Simulate a two-dimensional cumulative wear field under random weight, crowding, direction, ground-reaction force, sliding distance, and foot-position draws.
models.section: Algorithm 1 stair wear Monte Carlo simulation
strengths: Exposes the stochastic draw order and the spatial accumulation target rather than describing Monte Carlo only in prose.
models.summary: Algorithm 1 receives geometry, material, traffic, body-weight, crowding, and direction inputs; samples pedestrians across time; calls GRF, sliding-distance, and position generators; and accumulates alpha times force-distance divided by hardness with environmental correction into a wear grid.
validation_refs: Physical page 18 Algorithm 1 and physical pages 19-20 wear-field/life outputs were reconciled; the comparison remains an internal simulation demonstration.
